result.title: Few Trials, Many Metrics: Beta Mixtures for Low-Budget AI Evaluation
result.summary: Evaluating a stochastic AI system often requires many repeated samples per instance, especially for metrics defined over long horizons. Recent work has shown that modeling instance-level success probabilities with a Beta distribution recovers Pass@$k$ from far fewer samples than direct estimation. We show that this framework supports a broader range of evaluation targets. We fit a mixture of Beta distributions by marginal maximum likelihood, with the number of components chosen by BIC. From that one fit, we compute Pass$^k$ and AUC@$k$ at any horizon in closed form. We also derive delta-method confidence intervals for these metrics and for Pass@$k$, which require no additional model calls. Treating configurations rather than tasks as instances extends the same model to sensitivity analysis. For repeated success metrics, we find that mixture priors yield more accurate estimators than naive estimation across competition mathematics and graduate-level science benchmarks when extrapolating beyond the observed number of trials, and the resulting intervals cover the full-data reference. When prompts are treated as instances, it estimates the distribution of prompt sensitivity more accurately than a comparable item-response baseline without external covariates. Direct estimators remain preferable once trials reach the target horizon.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把实例级成功概率建模为 Beta 混合分布（边际极大似然拟合、BIC 选分量数），由一次拟合闭式得到任意 horizon 的 Pass^k 与 AUC@k，并给出 delta 法置信区间，还把配置而非任务视为实例以做敏感性分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 其少样本外推长程成功率与 prompt 敏感性的估计框架，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等配置收益的低预算比较与不确定度报告提供工具，可供核查其对视觉多模态基准与多次采样相关性的适用性。
